claims.falsification_next_step: Repeat the signed offset sweep across multiple official and real trajectories with independent seeds.
claims.scope: OpenVINS v2.7, one deterministic official simulation trajectory, fixed offsets from minus 50 ms to plus 50 ms.
claims.statement: Disabling online temporal calibration caused broad catastrophic trajectory divergence in all eight tested nonzero offsets; the worst maximum error was 506181.948762 m.
claims.title: Fixed camera-to-IMU timing mismatch is the strongest tested failure mode

claims.falsification_next_step: Test whether convergence remains stable when visual information is sparse, bursty or weakly exciting.
claims.scope: Same trajectory and measurement realization as the paired fixed-calibration experiment.
claims.statement: Online temporal calibration prevented catastrophic failure across all tested signed offsets, but the worst calibration-aware RMSE remained 0.321499900 m.
claims.title: Online temporal calibration is protective but not cost-free

claims.falsification_next_step: Estimate the breakpoint with denser dropout fractions, multiple seeds and different trajectories.
claims.scope: Random visual frame dropout on one deterministic official trajectory.
claims.statement: Random visual dropout showed a sharp tested degradation region near 30 percent, where the nearest scenario had an RMSE ratio of 3.724768304; the worst tested ratio was 4.080727788.
claims.title: Random visual dropout has a practical degradation breakpoint

claims.falsification_next_step: Repeat burst timing sweeps with multiple outage lengths and motion-excitation conditions.
claims.scope: One deterministic trajectory, selected burst start times and one-second or three-second outages.
claims.statement: Visual burst impact depended strongly on outage timing; the worst local RMSE ratio reached 3.065839800, showing that full-run RMSE can hide severe local failure.
claims.title: Local outage metrics reveal failures hidden by global RMSE

claims.falsification_next_step: Compare nominal and matched degraded estimator noise models, then repeat across independent seeds.
claims.scope: Unmodelled white-noise and random-walk increases up to ten times nominal on one trajectory.
claims.statement: Severe IMU noise-model mismatch increased RMSE and NEES without producing sustained one-metre service failure; the all-10x mean position NEES was 10.350944254.
claims.title: IMU noise mismatch degrades consistency before service collapse

claims.falsification_next_step: Re-estimate the risk ordering on real datasets and multi-trajectory simulation ensembles.
claims.scope: Only the degradation ranges and deterministic trajectory included in VeraNav v1.
claims.statement: The tested risk ordering was fixed temporal mismatch, high random visual dropout, adverse visual burst timing, then severe unmodelled IMU noise.
claims.title: Cross-factor reliability risk is strongly nonuniform

claims.falsification_next_step: Use multi-seed confidence intervals to determine whether small apparent improvements persist.
claims.scope: Single deterministic measurement realization and one trajectory.
claims.statement: Several low-severity perturbations produced nonmonotonic RMSE changes. These observations are not evidence that added noise or timing error improves localization.
claims.title: Single-run nonmonotonicity must not be overinterpreted

claims.falsification_next_step: Build multi-seed and multi-trajectory ensembles with predefined confidence intervals and effect-size models.
claims.scope: Methodological conclusion about the present evidence base, not a sensor-performance claim.
claims.statement: The v1 evidence is internally deterministic and strongly traceable, but population-level reliability and formal statistical consistency remain unproven.
claims.title: Deterministic reproducibility is not population-level validation
